title: Analysis of the Relationship Between Magnetization Work and Internal Energy Change in Adiabatic Cyclic Phase Transitions of Objects
content: This paper comprehensively analyzes the magnetization work exerted on objects during phase transitions and their heat absorption/release characteristics in superconducting and Curie phase transition cycles. By comparing and analyzing the thermodynamic processes of two adiabatic phase transitions in a varying magnetic field, it reveals that the energy conversion in both phase transitions is fundamentally similar. Specifically, after a complete adiabatic phase transition cycle, both superconductors and ferromagnets return to their initial states without accumulated magnetization work, the net heat exchange is zero, internal energy is conserved, and there is no net thermal energy exchange with the external environment, indicating no energy consumption in the phase transition cycle.
